newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up after late buying.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up after late buying.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended higher Friday in a moderate session, helped by a late wave of pre-weekend short covering after some technical weakness early in the session, market sources said.
July firmed 1.4 cents to close at $2.235 per million British thermal units. August settled 0.2 cent higher at $2.235. Other deferreds ended steady to up by one cent.

"The market bounced back from some early weakness on short covering ahead of the weekend. I still think the bias is up. The weather is a little supportive and should be enough to hold the physical and paper markets," a Midwest trader said.
Traders said the arrival in the Midwest and Northeast of the season's first heat wave triggered decent buying this week. But they said more seasonal forecasts later next week should temper the bulls.

Chart traders saw the new range in July between the double bottom at $2.151 and the double top at $2.245. Next resistance in July was pegged along a down trendline in the $2.28 area and then at the recent $2.365-$2.37. More buying was likely at $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

In the news, El Paso Natural Gas Co's Blanco gas plant in the San Juan Basin was expected to be back this weekend. On Friday and Saturday, 240 mmcfd will still be cut but on Sunday operations will return to normal. The Blanco plant normally processes about one bcfd.

In the weekend cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed slightly Friday to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were steady to down slightly at $2.05. New York city gate gas was quoted up slightly in the high-$2.40s on some hotter weather there.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 0.8 cent to $2.284. NYMEX said 39,837 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 51,602.

On the KCBT, July finished up one cent at $2.10, while deferreds ended one to four cents lower. The East/West spread widenwed by 0.4 cent to 13.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 182 lots traded, up slightly from Thursday's total of 179.
